3.71.s:
3.351
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
sa dadarśa tadā viṣṇuṃ viśvarūpadharaṃ harim ..
yuktaṃ varṇaiḥ śukaprakhyaiḥ pītaraktasitāsitaiḥ .. 1 ..
3.71.d:
3.351
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
स ददर्श तदा विष्णुं विश्वरूपधरं हरिम् ॥
युक्तं वर्णैः शुकप्रख्यैः पीतरक्तसितासितैः ॥ 1 ॥
3.71.m:
3.351
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
He then saw Viṣṇu Hari bearing his universal form, / endowed with colors resembling parrots, yellow, red, white, and black,

3.71.s:
kvacinmecakasaṃyuktaiḥ kvacinmecakarañjitaiḥ ..
cicchaśāṃkasaṃkāśaṃ kvaciddhiṅgulasannibham .. .. 2 ..
3.71.d:
क्वचिन्मेचकसंयुक्तैः क्वचिन्मेचकरञ्जितैः ॥
चिच्छशांकसंकाशं क्वचिद्धिङ्गुलसन्निभम् ॥ ॥ 2 ॥
3.71.m: here and there mingled with dark blue, here and there stained with dark blue, / shining like the pure moon, and in some places resembling cinnabar,

3.71.s:
kvacinmarakataprakhyaṃ padmarāganibhaṃ kvacit ..
kvacitkanakasaṃkāśaṃ kvacinnīlotpalaprabham .. 3 ..
3.71.d:
क्वचिन्मरकतप्रख्यं पद्मरागनिभं क्वचित् ॥
क्वचित्कनकसंकाशं क्वचिन्नीलोत्पलप्रभम् ॥ 3 ॥
3.71.m: in some places resembling emerald, in some places like ruby; / in some places resembling gold, in some places with the splendor of a blue lotus;

3.71.s:
kvacitpāṭalapuṣpābhaṃ kvacidgaganasannibham ..
kuṃkumakṣodasaṃkāśaṃ haridrakṣodasannibham .. 4 ..
3.71.d:
क्वचित्पाटलपुष्पाभं क्वचिद्गगनसन्निभम् ॥
कुंकुमक्षोदसंकाशं हरिद्रक्षोदसन्निभम् ॥ 4 ॥
3.71.m: in some places possessing the luster of the pāṭalā flower, in others resembling the sky, / like saffron powder and like turmeric powder;

3.71.s:
kvacidrajopalaprakhyamindranīlanibhaṃ kvacit ..
anirdeśyāni varṇāni tathā bibhratkvacitkvacit .. 5 ..
3.71.d:
क्वचिद्रजोपलप्रख्यमिन्द्रनीलनिभं क्वचित् ॥
अनिर्देश्यानि वर्णानि तथा बिभ्रत्क्वचित्क्वचित् ॥ 5 ॥
3.71.m: in some places resembling a silver-stone, in some places like a sapphire; / and likewise displaying indescribable colors in various places;

3.71.s:
nānāvidhānāṃ sattvānāṃ vadanāni bahūni ca ..
brahmaśaṃkaraśakrāṇāṃ yamasya varuṇasya ca .. 6 ..
3.71.d:
नानाविधानां सत्त्वानां वदनानि बहूनि च ॥
ब्रह्मशंकरशक्राणां यमस्य वरुणस्य च ॥ 6 ॥
3.71.m: and [he saw] many faces of various kinds of beings: / of Brahmā, Śaṃkara, and Indra, and of Yama and Varuṇa;

3.71.s:
dhanadasya hutāśasya vāyornirṛtinastathā ..
grahāṇāmatha ṛkṣāṇāṃ rudrāṇāṃ vasubhiḥ saha .. 7 ..
3.71.d:
धनदस्य हुताशस्य वायोर्निरृतिनस्तथा ॥
ग्रहाणामथ ऋक्षाणां रुद्राणां वसुभिः सह ॥ 7 ॥
3.71.m: [and the forms] of Dhanada, of Fire, of Wind, and likewise of Nirṛti, / of the planets and constellations, of the Rudras together with the Vasus,

3.71.s:
ādityānāṃ samarutāṃ bhṛgūṇāṃ ca tathā dvija ..
tathaivāṅgiraso rājansādhyānāmaśvibhiḥ saha .. 8 ..
3.71.d:
आदित्यानां समरुतां भृगूणां च तथा द्विज ॥
तथैवाङ्गिरसो राजन्साध्यानामश्विभिः सह ॥ 8 ॥
3.71.m: of the Ādityas with the Maruts, and likewise of the Bhṛgus, O twice-born one; / just so of the Aṅgirases, O king, and of the Sādhyas together with the Aśvins;

3.71.s:
daityānāmatha nānānāṃ gandharvoragarakṣasām ..
pitṛpannagayakṣāṇāṃ tathā ca piśitāśinām .. 9 ..
3.71.d:
दैत्यानामथ नानानां गन्धर्वोरगरक्षसाम् ॥
पितृपन्नगयक्षाणां तथा च पिशिताशिनाम् ॥ 9 ॥
3.71.m: and of various Daityas, Gandharvas, Uragas, and Rakṣases, / of ancestors, serpents, and Yakṣas, and likewise of flesh-eaters,

3.71.s:
manuṣya hayanāgānāṃ gajāśvamṛgapakṣiṇām ..
dvīpiśārdūlasiṃhānāṃ sarveṣāṃ prāṇināmatha .. 3.351.10 ..
3.71.d:
मनुष्य हयनागानां गजाश्वमृगपक्षिणाम् ॥
द्वीपिशार्दूलसिंहानां सर्वेषां प्राणिनामथ ॥ 3.351.10 ॥
3.71.m: of humans, horses, and elephants, of elephants, horses, beasts, and birds, / of leopards, tigers, and lions, and indeed of all living beings.

3.71.s:
kānicittasya saumyāni kānicidbhīṣaṇāni ca ..
dadarśa tasya vaktrāṇi śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ .. 11 ..
3.71.d:
कानिचित्तस्य सौम्यानि कानिचिद्भीषणानि च ॥
ददर्श तस्य वक्त्राणि शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः ॥ 11 ॥
3.71.m: Some of his faces were gentle, and some were terrifying; / he beheld his mouths by the hundreds and by the thousands.

3.71.s:
vaktreṣu tasya raudrasya prāṇisaṃghānyanekaśaḥ ..
dadarśa sarvataścāgnīngrasyamānām̐śca viṣṇunā ..12..
3.71.d:
वक्त्रेषु तस्य रौद्रस्य प्राणिसंघान्यनेकशः ॥
ददर्श सर्वतश्चाग्नीन्ग्रस्यमानाम्̐श्च विष्णुना ॥12॥
3.71.m: In the mouths of that terrible one he saw multitudes of living beings in great numbers, / and all around he saw fires being swallowed up by Viṣṇu.

3.71.s:
saumyebhyastasya vaktrebhyo nirgacchaṃtyastathā prajāḥ ..
vāhāṃśca vividhām̐stasya sa dadarśātha nāradaḥ .. 13..
3.71.d:
सौम्येभ्यस्तस्य वक्त्रेभ्यो निर्गच्छंत्यस्तथा प्रजाः ॥
वाहांश्च विविधाम्̐स्तस्य स ददर्शाथ नारदः ॥ 13॥
3.71.m: And likewise Nārada then saw creatures coming forth / from his gentle mouths, and his various mounts,

3.71.s:
hastām̐śca vividhākārānnānāmudrāsamanvitān ..
yuktānnānāvidhairbhāṇḍairāyudhaiśca sahasraśaḥ..14..
3.71.d:
हस्ताम्̐श्च विविधाकारान्नानामुद्रासमन्वितान् ॥
युक्तान्नानाविधैर्भाण्डैरायुधैश्च सहस्रशः॥14॥
3.71.m: and his hands of diverse shapes, furnished with various gestures, / equipped with diverse vessels and with weapons by the thousands,

3.71.s:
sruksruvāvedicamasakuśakṛṣṇājināgnibhiḥ ..
kecicca kalaśaṃ ghaṇṭāṃ śaṅkhapadmotpalādibhiḥ..15..
3.71.d:
स्रुक्स्रुवावेदिचमसकुशकृष्णाजिनाग्निभिः ॥
केचिच्च कलशं घण्टां शङ्खपद्मोत्पलादिभिः॥15॥
3.71.m: with oblation-ladles, offering-spoons, altars, sacrificial cups, kuśa grass, black antelope skins, and fires; / and some with water-pots, bells, conches, lotuses, blue water-lilies, and the like;

3.71.s:
kecitkhaḍgagadācakracarmaśūlaparaśvadhaiḥ ..
kecitpāśamahādaṇḍakṛpāṇaśarakārmukaiḥ .. 16 ..
3.71.d:
केचित्खड्गगदाचक्रचर्मशूलपरश्वधैः ॥
केचित्पाशमहादण्डकृपाणशरकार्मुकैः ॥ 16 ॥
3.71.m: some with swords, clubs, discuses, shields, tridents, and battle-axes; / some with nooses, great rods, daggers, arrows, and bows;

3.71.s:
kecidbhuśuṇḍīlaguḍaśaktivajrāśmapaṭṭiśaiḥ ..
bījapūrṇākṣamālāśca pūrṇapātraistathā paraiḥ .. 17 ..
3.71.d:
केचिद्भुशुण्डीलगुडशक्तिवज्राश्मपट्टिशैः ॥
बीजपूर्णाक्षमालाश्च पूर्णपात्रैस्तथा परैः ॥ 17 ॥
3.71.m: some with bhuśuṇḍī-missiles, cudgels, spears, thunderbolts, sling-stones, and barbed darts; / and others with citrons, rosaries, and full vessels.

3.71.s:
evaṃ nānāvidhairbhāṇḍaiḥ karāṃstasya samanvitān ..
asaṃkhyeyānmahātejā dadarśa munisattamaḥ .. 18 ..
3.71.d:
एवं नानाविधैर्भाण्डैः करांस्तस्य समन्वितान् ॥
असंख्येयान्महातेजा ददर्श मुनिसत्तमः ॥ 18 ॥
3.71.m: Thus the most excellent sage of great splendor beheld / his innumerable hands furnished with various kinds of implements.

3.71.s:
nṛttaśāstravinirdiṣṭo nṛttakarmaṇi cāpyatha ..
śirāṃsi dṛṣṭayo hastāṃstasya devasya dṛṣṭavān .. 19 ..
3.71.d:
नृत्तशास्त्रविनिर्दिष्टो नृत्तकर्मणि चाप्यथ ॥
शिरांसि दृष्टयो हस्तांस्तस्य देवस्य दृष्टवान् ॥ 19 ॥
3.71.m: And then he saw the heads, glances, and hands of that god, / as prescribed in the treatise on dance and employed in the performance of dance.

3.71.s:
trailokyaṃ ca tathā kāye sakalaṃ munisattamaḥ ..
devadānavagandharvasayakṣoragarakṣasām .. 3.351.20 ..
3.71.d:
त्रैलोक्यं च तथा काये सकलं मुनिसत्तमः ॥
देवदानवगन्धर्वसयक्षोरगरक्षसाम् ॥ 3.351.20 ॥
3.71.m: and likewise the best of sages [saw] the entire triple world in his body, / [consisting] of gods, Dānavas, Gandharvas, along with Yakṣas, Uragas, and Rakṣases.

3.71.s:
dvīpāmbhonidhilokaiśca pātālaiścaiva saṃyutam ..
jagatsamagraṃ devasya dehasthaṃ dṛṣṭavānmuniḥ .. 21 ..
3.71.d:
द्वीपाम्भोनिधिलोकैश्च पातालैश्चैव संयुतम् ॥
जगत्समग्रं देवस्य देहस्थं दृष्टवान्मुनिः ॥ 21 ॥
3.71.m: the sage beheld the whole universe residing in the body of the god, / together with the continents, the oceans, the worlds, and the nether regions.

3.71.s:
sa dṛṣṭvā paramaṃ rūpaṃ bhīto hṛṣṭaśca vismitaḥ ..
papāta pādayostasya śirasā sāśrulocanaḥ .. 22 ..
3.71.d:
स दृष्ट्वा परमं रूपं भीतो हृष्टश्च विस्मितः ॥
पपात पादयोस्तस्य शिरसा साश्रुलोचनः ॥ 22 ॥
3.71.m: Having seen that supreme form, frightened, rejoiced, and filled with wonder, / he fell at his feet with his head bowed, his eyes filled with tears.

3.71.s:
stotreṇa caiva tuṣṭāva pūrvoktena janārdanam ..
tamuvāca tato devaḥ prahasannṛṣisattamam .. 23 ..
3.71.d:
स्तोत्रेण चैव तुष्टाव पूर्वोक्तेन जनार्दनम् ॥
तमुवाच ततो देवः प्रहसन्नृषिसत्तमम् ॥ 23 ॥
3.71.m: And he praised Janārdana with the previously spoken hymn of praise; / then the god, gently smiling, said to that best of ṛṣis:

3.71.s:
.. śrībhagavānuvāca .. ..
uttiṣṭha mābhairdharmajña varaṃ vṛṇu yathepsitam ..
.. śrīnārada uvāca .. ..
nityamekāntike deva bhaktirbhavatu sā tvayi ..
nānyaṃ varaṃ kāmayāmi narāṇāmidamuttamam .. 24 ..
3.71.d:
॥ श्रीभगवानुवाच ॥ ॥
उत्तिष्ठ माभैर्धर्मज्ञ वरं वृणु यथेप्सितम् ॥
॥ श्रीनारद उवाच ॥ ॥
नित्यमेकान्तिके देव भक्तिर्भवतु सा त्वयि ॥
नान्यं वरं कामयामि नराणामिदमुत्तमम् ॥ 24 ॥
3.71.m:
The Blessed Lord said:
"Arise, fear not, O knower of dharma! Choose a boon as you desire."
Illustrious Nārada said:
"O Lord, let there be perpetual, single-minded devotion to you; / I desire no other boon; this is the highest for men."

3.71.s:
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca .. ..
tamuvāca tato devaḥ praṇatārtiharo hariḥ ..
etannisargasiddhaṃ te yena tvaṃ dṛṣṭavānmama .. 25 ..
3.71.d:
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥ ॥
तमुवाच ततो देवः प्रणतार्तिहरो हरिः ॥
एतन्निसर्गसिद्धं ते येन त्वं दृष्टवान्मम ॥ 25 ॥
3.71.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Then the god, Hari, remover of the distress of those who bow to him, spoke to him:
“This has been achieved by your nature, whereby you have seen my

3.71.s:
viśvarūpamidaṃ brahmannavajñeyaṃ tathā tvayā ..
tapastaptaṃ yato vipra mamāpi ca tatastava .. 26 ..
3.71.d:
विश्वरूपमिदं ब्रह्मन्नवज्ञेयं तथा त्वया ॥
तपस्तप्तं यतो विप्र ममापि च ततस्तव ॥ 26 ॥
3.71.m:
universal form, O Brahmin, which is so difficult to know.
Because austerity was performed [by you], O Brahmin, and therefore [it was shown] by me to you.”

3.71.s:
rūpametatsamāsthāya rūpaṃ svaṃ dvija darśitam ..
icchārūpāṇyahaṃ kuryāṃ śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ .. 27 ..
3.71.d:
रूपमेतत्समास्थाय रूपं स्वं द्विज दर्शितम् ॥
इच्छारूपाण्यहं कुर्यां शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः ॥ 27 ॥
3.71.m: Resorting to this form, O twice-born, my own form has been shown [to you]. / I can assume willed forms by the hundreds and by the thousands.

3.71.s:
trailokye yāni rūpāṇi devādīnāṃ dvijottama ..
mamaiva tāni jānīhi matto'nyannāsti kiñcana .. 28 ..
3.71.d:
त्रैलोक्ये यानि रूपाणि देवादीनां द्विजोत्तम ॥
ममैव तानि जानीहि मत्तोऽन्यन्नास्ति किञ्चन ॥ 28 ॥
3.71.m: "Whatever forms of gods and other beings exist in the triple world, O best of the twice-born, / know that they are mine alone; there is nothing whatsoever other than me.

3.71.s:
ahaṃ bhūtaṃ ca bhavyaṃ ca vartamānamahaṃ tathā ..
sthāvaraṃ jaṅgamaṃ caiva sarvamevāsmi nārada .. 29 ..
3.71.d:
अहं भूतं च भव्यं च वर्तमानमहं तथा ॥
स्थावरं जङ्गमं चैव सर्वमेवास्मि नारद ॥ 29 ॥
3.71.m: I am the past, the future, and likewise the present; / I am indeed all that is immobile and mobile, O Nārada.

3.71.s:
saccā'saccāhamevātra tattvametadbravīmi te ..
aśabdamarasaṃ sparśagandharūpavivarjitam .. 3.351.30 ..
3.71.d:
सच्चाऽसच्चाहमेवात्र तत्त्वमेतद्ब्रवीमि ते ॥
अशब्दमरसं स्पर्शगन्धरूपविवर्जितम् ॥ 3.351.30 ॥
3.71.m: I alone am the existent and the non-existent here; I tell you this truth: / Soundless, tasteless, devoid of touch, smell, and form,

3.71.s:
sarvagaṃ māṃ vijānīhi paramārthena nārada ..
yaḥ kariṣyati me stotraṃ stotreṇa tvatkṛtena tu .. 33 ..
3.71.d:
सर्वगं मां विजानीहि परमार्थेन नारद ॥
यः करिष्यति मे स्तोत्रं स्तोत्रेण त्वत्कृतेन तु ॥ 33 ॥
3.71.m: know me in ultimate truth to be all-pervading, O Nārada. / Whoever offers praise to me with the hymn composed by you,

3.71.s:
tasya kāmānvidhāsyāmi ye divyā ye ca mānuṣāḥ ..
śvetadvīpe gatistasya mṛtasya ca bhaviṣyati .. 32 ..
3.71.d:
तस्य कामान्विधास्यामि ये दिव्या ये च मानुषाः ॥
श्वेतद्वीपे गतिस्तस्य मृतस्य च भविष्यति ॥ 32 ॥
3.71.m: I shall fulfill his desires, both celestial and human, / and after death, his destination shall be Śvetadvīpa.

3.71.s:
śvetadvīpamavāpyāpi naraḥ svastho bhaviṣyasi ..
varāhasyāsya kalpasya yāvatkālo'vaśiṣyate .. 33
3.71.d:
श्वेतद्वीपमवाप्यापि नरः स्वस्थो भविष्यसि ॥
वराहस्यास्य कल्पस्य यावत्कालोऽवशिष्यते ॥ 33
3.71.m: Having reached Śvetadvīpa, you too, O man, will abide in your true nature, / as long as time remains in this Varāha kalpa.

3.71.s:
vārāhe tu gate kalpe tato mātsyo bhaviṣyati ..
devakāryāṇi kāryāṇi subahūni yatastvayā .. 34 ..
3.71.d:
वाराहे तु गते कल्पे ततो मात्स्यो भविष्यति ॥
देवकार्याणि कार्याणि सुबहूनि यतस्त्वया ॥ 34 ॥
3.71.m: When the Vārāha kalpa has passed, then the Mātsya [kalpa] will take place; / since very many duties for the gods are to be performed by you,

3.71.s:
prādurbhāvagataścāhamanuśāsyastathā tvayā ..
prādurbhāvāṇi me brahmanvyatītāni sahasraśaḥ .. 35 ..
3.71.d:
प्रादुर्भावगतश्चाहमनुशास्यस्तथा त्वया ॥
प्रादुर्भावाणि मे ब्रह्मन्व्यतीतानि सहस्रशः ॥ 35 ॥
3.71.m: and when I have entered manifestations, I am to be instructed by you. / My manifestations, O brahmin, that have passed are by the thousands;

3.71.s:
bhaviṣyanti tathānyāni tatra me śṛṇu kānicit ..
ahamekārṇave loke śeṣaparyaṃkaśāyikaḥ .. 36 ..
3.71.d:
भविष्यन्ति तथान्यानि तत्र मे शृणु कानिचित् ॥
अहमेकार्णवे लोके शेषपर्यंकशायिकः ॥ 36 ॥
3.71.m: Others will also come to be; hear about some of them from me. / When the world is a single ocean, lying on the couch of Śeṣa,

3.71.s:
lakṣmīsahāyastiṣṭhāmi yadā suptaḥ pitāmahaḥ ..
ahaṃ matsyastathā kūrmo haṃsohmapi nārada .. 37 ..
3.71.d:
लक्ष्मीसहायस्तिष्ठामि यदा सुप्तः पितामहः ॥
अहं मत्स्यस्तथा कूर्मो हंसोह्मपि नारद ॥ 37 ॥
3.71.m: accompanied by Lakṣmī, I remain while the Grandfather is asleep. / I am the Fish, and likewise the Tortoise, and I am also the Swan, O Nārada.

3.71.s:
strīrūpeṇa mayā vipra vañcitā daityadānavāḥ ..
mayāśvaśirasā vedā dānavebhyastathā hṛtāḥ .. 38 ..
3.71.d:
स्त्रीरूपेण मया विप्र वञ्चिता दैत्यदानवाः ॥
मयाश्वशिरसा वेदा दानवेभ्यस्तथा हृताः ॥ 38 ॥
3.71.m: In female form, O brahmin, the Daityas and Dānavas were deceived by me; / in horse-headed form, the Vedas were likewise recovered by me from the Dānavas.

3.71.s:
vārāheṇa mayā bhūtvā vasudheyaṃ samuddhṛtā ..
vārāheṇa mayā daityāḥ pātālatalagā hatāḥ .. 39 ..
3.71.d:
वाराहेण मया भूत्वा वसुधेयं समुद्धृता ॥
वाराहेण मया दैत्याः पातालतलगा हताः ॥ 39 ॥
3.71.m: Having become the Boar, this earth was lifted up by me; / as the Boar, the Daityas dwelling in the depths of Pātāla were slain by me.

3.71.s:
nṛvarāheṇa nihato hiraṇyākṣo balotkaṭaḥ ..
dānavāśca hatā yuddhe naranārāyaṇātmanā .. 3.351.40 ..
3.71.d:
नृवराहेण निहतो हिरण्याक्षो बलोत्कटः ॥
दानवाश्च हता युद्धे नरनारायणात्मना ॥ 3.351.40 ॥
3.71.m: Hiraṇyākṣa of vehement might was slain by the Man-Boar; / and the Dānavas were slain in battle by the self of Nara-Nārāyaṇa.

3.71.s:
lokottare tathā mārge hariḥ kṛṣṇastathāpyaham ..
nārasiṃhena rūpeṇa hiraṇyakaśipurhataḥ .. 41 ..
3.71.d:
लोकोत्तरे तथा मार्गे हरिः कृष्णस्तथाप्यहम् ॥
नारसिंहेन रूपेण हिरण्यकशिपुर्हतः ॥ 41 ॥
3.71.m: Likewise, in the transcendent path, I am Hari and Kṛṣṇa; / in the Man-Lion form, Hiraṇyakaśipu was slain.

3.71.s:
vāmanena mayā bhūtvā balestribhuvanaṃ hṛtam ..
tribhiḥ kramaiḥ purā brahmandevānāṃ hitakāmyayā .. 42 ..
3.71.d:
वामनेन मया भूत्वा बलेस्त्रिभुवनं हृतम् ॥
त्रिभिः क्रमैः पुरा ब्रह्मन्देवानां हितकाम्यया ॥ 42 ॥
3.71.m: Having become Vāmana, the three worlds were seized from Bali by me / with three strides formerly, O brahmin, desiring the welfare of the gods.

3.71.s:
vāḍavo'haṃ samudrasthaḥ pibāmi salilaṃ sadā ..
pṛthvī vasumatī brahmanpṛthunā ca mayā kṛtā .. 43 ..
3.71.d:
वाडवोऽहं समुद्रस्थः पिबामि सलिलं सदा ॥
पृथ्वी वसुमती ब्रह्मन्पृथुना च मया कृता ॥ 43 ॥
3.71.m: I am the submarine fire abiding in the ocean, constantly drinking the water; / and the earth was made wealthy, O brahmin, by me as Pṛthu.

3.71.s:
kāpilena mayā duṣṭā dagdhavyāḥ sagarātmajāḥ ..
dattātreyeṇa vasudhā devā dvijagaṇāḥ punaḥ .. 44 ..
3.71.d:
कापिलेन मया दुष्टा दग्धव्याः सगरात्मजाः ॥
दत्तात्रेयेण वसुधा देवा द्विजगणाः पुनः ॥ 44 ॥
3.71.m: By me as Kapila the wicked sons of Sagara are to be burnt; / by [me as] Dattātreya, the earth, the gods, and the hosts of the twice-born again [are to be protected].

3.71.s:
jāmadagnyena rāmeṇa laghvī vasumatī kṛtā ..
trisapta kṛtvaḥ kartavyā kṣatrabhāraprapīḍitā .. 45 ..
3.71.d:
जामदग्न्येन रामेण लघ्वी वसुमती कृता ॥
त्रिसप्त कृत्वः कर्तव्या क्षत्रभारप्रपीडिता ॥ 45 ॥
3.71.m: By Rāma, son of Jamadagni, the earth is made light; / thrice seven times it must be made so, oppressed by the burden of the kṣatriyas.

3.71.s:
dattvā caturdhā putrām̐śca mayā daśarathasya ca ..
rāmeṇa rāvaṇavadhaḥ kartavyo janatāsukham .. 46 ..
3.71.d:
दत्त्वा चतुर्धा पुत्राम्̐श्च मया दशरथस्य च ॥
रामेण रावणवधः कर्तव्यो जनतासुखम् ॥ 46 ॥
3.71.m: And giving myself fourfold as sons to Daśaratha, / the slaying of Rāvaṇa must be performed by me as Rāma for the happiness of the people.

3.71.s:
kāryaṃ gandharvanidhanaṃ tathaiva bharatātmanā ..
meghanādavadhaḥ kāryo lakṣmaṇena tathā mayā ..47..
3.71.d:
कार्यं गन्धर्वनिधनं तथैव भरतात्मना ॥
मेघनादवधः कार्यो लक्ष्मणेन तथा मया ॥47॥
3.71.m: Likewise, the destruction of the Gandharvas is to be carried out through the form of Bharata; / the slaying of Meghanāda is likewise to be performed by me as Lakṣmaṇa.

3.71.s:
śatrughnena ca karttavyo lavaṇasya vadhastathā..
mayā vālmīkinā kāryaṃ kāvyaṃ rāmāyaṇaṃ tathā ..48..
3.71.d:
शत्रुघ्नेन च कर्त्तव्यो लवणस्य वधस्तथा॥
मया वाल्मीकिना कार्यं काव्यं रामायणं तथा ॥48॥
3.71.m: And the slaying of Lavaṇa must be performed by Śatrughna; / by me as Vālmīki the poetic composition Rāmāyaṇa must be composed."

3.71.s:
vyāsen vedā vaktavyā ākhyānaṃ bhārataṃ mahat ..
mayā brāhmaṇaśārdūla tathā dvaipāyanātmanā..49..
3.71.d:
व्यासेन् वेदा वक्तव्या आख्यानं भारतं महत् ॥
मया ब्राह्मणशार्दूल तथा द्वैपायनात्मना॥49॥
3.71.m: The Vedas are to be spoken by Vyāsa, and the great Bhārata story, / by Me, O tiger among brahmins, in the form of Dvaipāyana.

3.71.s:
pāṇḍoḥ putratvamāsādya pañcadhā ca tathā mayā ..
dvidhā ca vasudevasya laghvī kāryā vasundharā ..3.351.50..
3.71.d:
पाण्डोः पुत्रत्वमासाद्य पञ्चधा च तथा मया ॥
द्विधा च वसुदेवस्य लघ्वी कार्या वसुन्धरा ॥3.351.50॥
3.71.m: Having attained sonship to Pāṇḍu in five ways, and likewise by Me / in two ways [as the son] of Vasudeva, the earth must be made light.

3.71.s:
naraloke nihantavyā daityā mānuṣarūpiṇaḥ ..
balabhadreṇa ca mayā hantavyā mauṣṭikādayaḥ .. 51 ..
3.71.d:
नरलोके निहन्तव्या दैत्या मानुषरूपिणः ॥
बलभद्रेण च मया हन्तव्या मौष्टिकादयः ॥ 51 ॥
3.71.m: The Daityas in human form are to be slain in the world of mortals; / and by me as Balabhadra, Mauṣṭika and others are to be slain.

3.71.s:
mayā kṛṣṇena hantavyāḥ kaṃsapūrvā mahābalāḥ ..
pradyumnena nihantavyaḥ śambaraśca mahābalaḥ .. 52 ...
3.71.d:
मया कृष्णेन हन्तव्याः कंसपूर्वा महाबलाः ॥
प्रद्युम्नेन निहन्तव्यः शम्बरश्च महाबलः ॥ 52 ॥।
3.71.m: By me as Kṛṣṇa, Kaṃsa and the other mighty ones are to be slain; / and by Pradyumna, Śambara of great strength is to be slain.

3.71.s:
hantavyāścāniruddhena daityāḥ śatasahasraśaḥ ..
sāṃbena yuyudhānena mayā bhūtvā tathaiva ca ..53..
3.71.d:
हन्तव्याश्चानिरुद्धेन दैत्याः शतसहस्रशः ॥
सांबेन युयुधानेन मया भूत्वा तथैव च ॥53॥
3.71.m: And hundreds of thousands of daityas are to be slain by Aniruddha, / by Sāmba, and by Yuyudhāna, by Me having thus become [them].

3.71.s:
mayā buddhena vaktavyā dharmāḥ kaliyuge punaḥ ..
hantavyā mleccharājānastathā viṣṇuvaśātmanā ..54..
3.71.d:
मया बुद्धेन वक्तव्या धर्माः कलियुगे पुनः ॥
हन्तव्या म्लेच्छराजानस्तथा विष्णुवशात्मना ॥54॥
3.71.m: the dharmas are to be declared by me as the Buddha in the Kali age; / again, the barbarian kings are to be slain through the self of Viṣṇuyaśas [son, Kalki].

3.71.s:
mamāṃśena vijānīhi pṛthivyāṃ cakravartinaḥ ..
ṛṣayaśca tathā jñeyā mamaivāṃśasamudbhavāḥ ..55..
3.71.d:
ममांशेन विजानीहि पृथिव्यां चक्रवर्तिनः ॥
ऋषयश्च तथा ज्ञेया ममैवांशसमुद्भवाः ॥55॥
3.71.m: Know the universal monarchs upon earth to be from a portion of me; / and the ṛṣis are to be known as originating from a portion of me alone.

3.71.s:
yadyadvibhūtimatsattvaṃ śrīmadūrjitameva ca ..
tattadevāvagacchestvaṃ mama tejoṃśasambhavam .. 56 ..
3.71.d:
यद्यद्विभूतिमत्सत्त्वं श्रीमदूर्जितमेव च ॥
तत्तदेवावगच्छेस्त्वं मम तेजोंशसम्भवम् ॥ 56 ॥
3.71.m: Whatever being possesses majesty, is endowed with glory, and is mighty, / understand that very being to have arisen from a portion of My splendour.

3.71.s:
atha vā bahunaitena kiṃ jñānena tavānagha ..
viṣṭabhyāhamidaṃ kṛtsnamekāṃśenāsthito jagat .. 57..
3.71.d:
अथ वा बहुनैतेन किं ज्ञानेन तवानघ ॥
विष्टभ्याहमिदं कृत्स्नमेकांशेनास्थितो जगत् ॥ 57॥
3.71.m: Or rather, what is the use of this extensive knowledge to you, O sinless one? / I abide supporting this entire universe with a single portion [of myself].

3.71.s:
tadgaccha mānasī siddhiḥ sadā te'stu dvijottama ..
kalpāvasānamāsādya maccharīraṃ pravekṣyasi .. 58 ..
3.71.d:
तद्गच्छ मानसी सिद्धिः सदा तेऽस्तु द्विजोत्तम ॥
कल्पावसानमासाद्य मच्छरीरं प्रवेक्ष्यसि ॥ 58 ॥
3.71.m: Therefore, go; may mental perfection always be yours, O best of the twice-born! / Reaching the end of the kalpa, you will enter my body.

3.71.s:
etāvaduktvā vacanaṃ tatraivāntaradhīyata ..
bhagavānnāradaścakre pūjāṃ taddeśavāsinām ..59..
3.71.d:
एतावदुक्त्वा वचनं तत्रैवान्तरधीयत ॥
भगवान्नारदश्चक्रे पूजां तद्देशवासिनाम् ॥59॥
3.71.m: Having spoken this much, the Lord disappeared right there. / Nārada performed worship of the dwellers of that region.

3.71.s:
taiśca saṃpūjito viprastānpraṇamya yatavrataḥ ..
ājagāma tataḥ śīghraṃ naranārāyaṇāśramam .. 3.351.60 ..
3.71.d:
तैश्च संपूजितो विप्रस्तान्प्रणम्य यतव्रतः ॥
आजगाम ततः शीघ्रं नरनारायणाश्रमम् ॥ 3.351.60 ॥
3.71.m: And honoured by them, the twice-born sage, firm in his vows, having bowed to them, / went from there swiftly to the hermitage of Nara-Nārāyaṇa.

3.71.s:
pādayornyapatattatra sa tayormunipūjyayoḥ ..
tābhyāṃ saṃpūjito viprastatrovāsa tadāśrame .. 61 ..
3.71.d:
पादयोर्न्यपतत्तत्र स तयोर्मुनिपूज्ययोः ॥
ताभ्यां संपूजितो विप्रस्तत्रोवास तदाश्रमे ॥ 61 ॥
3.71.m: He fell there at the feet of the two who are revered by sages; / honoured by the two, the twice-born sage dwelt there in their hermitage.

3.71.s:
tataḥ kadācittaṃ vipramūcatustau tapodhanau ..
āvābhyāṃ tvaṃ tathā dṛṣṭaḥ śvetadvīpagate'cyutaḥ .. 62 ..
3.71.d:
ततः कदाचित्तं विप्रमूचतुस्तौ तपोधनौ ॥
आवाभ्यां त्वं तथा दृष्टः श्वेतद्वीपगतेऽच्युतः ॥ 62 ॥
3.71.m: Then on one occasion those two rich in austerity said to that twice-born sage: / "Acyuta was seen by you in Śvetadvīpa just as by us,

3.71.s:
samīpaṃ devadevasya taddehasthairyathāsukham ..
loke'sminmuniśārdūla nāsti dhanyatarastvayā .. 63 ..
3.71.d:
समीपं देवदेवस्य तद्देहस्थैर्यथासुखम् ॥
लोकेऽस्मिन्मुनिशार्दूल नास्ति धन्यतरस्त्वया ॥ 63 ॥
3.71.m: near the God of gods at ease, like those residing in his body; / in this world, O tiger among sages, no one is more blessed than you,

3.71.s:
dṛṣṭavānasi yadbrahmanviśvarūpadharaṃ harim ..
trailokyasāraṃ viśveśaṃ praṇatārtivināśanam .. 64 ..
3.71.d:
दृष्टवानसि यद्ब्रह्मन्विश्वरूपधरं हरिम् ॥
त्रैलोक्यसारं विश्वेशं प्रणतार्तिविनाशनम् ॥ 64 ॥
3.71.m: since, O brahmin, you have seen Hari who bears the universal form, / the essence of the three worlds, lord of the universe, destroyer of the distress of those who bow.

3.71.s:
yataste'nugrahastena kṛto devena viṣṇunā ..
tato guhyaṃ nibodhemaṃ tatpūjāvidhimuttamam .. 65 ..
3.71.d:
यतस्तेऽनुग्रहस्तेन कृतो देवेन विष्णुना ॥
ततो गुह्यं निबोधेमं तत्पूजाविधिमुत्तमम् ॥ 65 ॥
3.71.m: Since that grace was bestowed upon you by the god Viṣṇu, / therefore learn this secret, supreme rite of his worship,

3.71.s:
sarvakarmakaraṃ divyaṃ sakalārthapradaṃ śivam ..
nābhaktāya ca taddeyaṃ tvayā brāhmaṇasattama ..66..
3.71.d:
सर्वकर्मकरं दिव्यं सकलार्थप्रदं शिवम् ॥
नाभक्ताय च तद्देयं त्वया ब्राह्मणसत्तम ॥66॥
3.71.m: which accomplishes all tasks, is divine, yields all aims, and is auspicious; / and it should not be imparted by you to a non-devotee, O best of brahmins.

3.71.s:
ekāntabhāvopagataṃ janārdanaṃ narastu sampūjya tathā vidhānataḥ ..
prayāti taddvīpamanuttamaṃ śivaṃ na yatra gatvā vinivartate punaḥ .. 67..
3.71.d:
एकान्तभावोपगतं जनार्दनं नरस्तु सम्पूज्य तथा विधानतः ॥
प्रयाति तद्द्वीपमनुत्तमं शिवं न यत्र गत्वा विनिवर्तते पुनः ॥ 67॥
3.71.m: Having worshipped according to the rite Janārdana, who is attained through single-minded devotion, / a person proceeds to that supreme and auspicious island, having gone to which one does not return again.

3.71.s:

ऐशाने दले तदिति ब्रह्माणं विन्यसेत् पद्मपत्राभं ध्यायेत् ॥
सूर्यकोटिसमं ध्यायेत् ॥

शशाङ्कवर्णं ध्यायेत् ॥
घें हें भें हें श्रियं पद्मं दक्षिणतो न्यसेत् ।
शुक्लां ध्यायेत् ॥
गें डें वें शें पद्मान्तरतः पुष्टिं न्यसेत् ।
श्वेतां ध्यायेत् ।
हें सें पुरतो वनमालां न्यसेत् ।
हें सें बहुवर्णां ध्यायेत् ॥
ओं चित्यैशान्यां नन्दकं न्यसेत् ।
आकाशवर्णं ध्यायेत् ॥
ओंमित्याग्नेय्यां वर्म न्यसेत् ।
बहुवर्णं ध्यायेत् ॥
ओं क्षें लें श्रीवत्सं न्यसेत् ।
शुक्लां ध्यायेत्॥
ओं छें ठें वायव्ये कौस्तुभं न्यसेत् आदित्यं दीप्तं ध्यायेत्॥

यथोक्तरूपं ध्यायेत् ॥

Having caused sickness, it consumes the sick; he does not perform it, nor does he obtain it; this, however, is different: / it brings good fortune, fame, merit, purity, and destroys sin; / it brings health, increases wealth and grain, destroys enemies, and causes subjugation. The man who constantly worships the deity according to this rite produces prosperity; or, if that does not please him, then having attained Śvetadvīpa, having pierced the solar disc, he restrains [all]; he attains Pradyumna and Saṃkarṣaṇa, and having attained true divinity, he attains partlessness.
3.353
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Indeed, having heard this spoken by Nara and Nārāyaṇa, Nārada / [worshipped] Madhusūdana constantly by this very rite.
Then the Lord, the father of all, visibly spoke words to the great-souled Nārada who was present before him:
'Go, auspicious Nārada, travel the worlds as you desire; / I shall grant you sight [of myself] from time to time as desired.'

Having obtained this grace from Puruṣottama, the Lord of gods, / Nārada wandered the worlds, constantly worshipping Hari.
This universal form was seen by the great-souled Nārada; / and again by Prahlāda when [the Lord] had the form of the Man-Lion;
likewise in the immortal body by that same great soul; / and formerly it was seen by Brahmā during the striding across the three worlds;
again it was seen at the western ocean by the rākṣasa Daśagrīva; / and in the incarnation as Kṛṣṇa, when the foe of Madhu had gone as an envoy,
he was witnessed by the sages in the assembly of the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra; / and so Arjuna saw [it] in the Mahābhārata battle,
where, agitated by the fear of slaying his kinsmen, he was enlightened by him.
When the Bhārata war had ceased, as [Kṛṣṇa] was returning again to Dvārakā, / that was seen by the great-souled Uttaṅka who had arrived on the path.

3.354
Vajra said:
Concerning the majesty of the god of gods, Viṣṇu of immeasurable splendour, / there is no satiety; therefore tell me further majesty.
Of that very god of gods, Viṣṇu of immeasurable splendour, / [tell me] the supreme wonder among the worlds, which is endowed with protection and purifying.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
There was a certain foremost twice-born man who possessed single-minded devotion,
a Sātvata, the best of the Gautamas, known as Viṣvaksena, / who knew the rules of the five periods of the day and knew the Pāñcarātra rules.
He constantly worshipped Janārdana, the god of gods; / he wandered the earth in order to worship at temples of Kṛṣṇa.

3.71.m:
Once he reached a great mountain cavern, / where all the people were devoted to Maheśvara, born of his power, in great numbers.
Having bathed there in a waterfall, he worshipped Keśava; / on an altar that had been prepared, he [worshipped] the Lord with the offerings at hand.
Then someone, coming out of that cavern by chance, / accompanied by many men armed with swords and holding bows in their hands,
saw him worshipping Janārdana. / Approaching him, the village chieftain's son
said to him: “Come here and perform the service of the gods for me. / Afflicted with a headache, dear sir, I am unable to bathe today.
Since I am unable to perform the divine rites, dear sir, worship Śaṅkara; / having gone to the divine shrine, dear sir, where
the established liṅga of Mahādeva, the lord of the gods, stands.” / When this was spoken, he replied: “We are known as worshippers of the One [God].
Hari, possessing four souls, or manifesting in descents, is to be worshipped; / I will not worship any other today; therefore go without delay.”

3.71.m:
Addressed thus, the youth drew his sword quickly / and then said to that brahmin: “I shall kill you, there is no doubt,
if you do not go and perform the worship of the liṅga, fool! / There is no single god greater than the sword, lowest of men!
With this sword I will strike off your head, without doubt!” / Thus addressed by him, intent on protecting his life,
saying, “I will go outside there,” he then went along with him. / And seeing the liṅga of the god, the knower of dharma reflected:
“Viṣṇu is the all-pervading god, the self of all, Madhusūdana; / by his terrible aspect Mahādeva is established.
And by that fierce aspect of his, the lord is Narasiṃha; / in this liṅga I shall worship the god of gods, the Great Self, / who bears the form of Narasiṃha. Therefore, through the constant worship of gods,
there will be no transgression, and the desired protection of life [will be achieved].” / Then, having mentally meditated upon that lord of the god of gods

3.355 / Vajra said: / That hymn by which Madhusūdana was praised by the Sāttvata, / recite that hymn to me, which destroys all impurities.

3.71.m: Oṃ, homage to the blessed Vāsudeva! Homage to Narasiṃha, the primal deity, supreme over all worlds, to Nārāyaṇa whose majesty of power, strength, valor, and splendor is ever at hand to be attained; whose body has the brilliance of a great mountain of silver; who has large manes of hair; whose golden complexion shines with radiant luster, raised and copper-colored on the auspicious crown; whose forehead is curved with knit brows arisen to remove the distress of people who have surrendered to him; whose throat darts forth flashes bright as swirling lightning; whose rolling, tawny, round eyes blaze like flaming fire; who controls breath fearful to cities, accompanied by prominent flat arteries; whose cheeks are throbbing and full on both sides; whose very terrible, white, extremely sharp fangs gleam and issue from lips shaped like the crescent moon; whose exceedingly terrifying roar is like the rumbling of masses of clouds and the fall of a thousand thunderbolts agitating the gatherings of all directions; whose body shines with the radiance of the sky colored by twilight glowing with stars, while a row of teeth with pure points is seen again and again occupying the terrible half of his mouth; whose throat, rounded, thick, and lovely like a conch, is firmly established in the middle of his broad shoulders, collarbones, and nape, which are steadfastly joined with the tip of his trembling creeper-like tongue on his palate; whose broad chest is adorned with the mark of the Śrīvatsa; who wears a pendant garland woven of various lovely, supremely fragrant loose flowers; whose formidable and terrifying weapons are the claws on the palms, wrists, and upraised, mighty arms victorious through strength rivaling the course of the winds and the sun; whose sharp diamond-hard weapon drank the blood of Hiraṇyakaśipu; whose waist is bound with a girdle of supreme yellow silk cloth; who is the primal deity, the Cosmic Person Narasiṃha, whose waist, thighs, and knees have joints that are firmly knit like a thunderbolt, upraised, durable, and well-joined; who possesses great speed and the swiftness of mighty arms, with deep-set ankle-joints of slender form extended as fitting for his steadfast and devout devotees; the surface of the earth being shaken by the power of his stepping feet; who bears the shadow of a clump of supremely auspicious body-hairs shaped like the auspicious tree, conch, discus, mace, throne, nandyāvarta, banner, elephant-goad, parasol, mirror, fish, tortoise, waves, sacrificial post, moon, sun, bull, horse, elephant, chariot, and the Supreme Person; whose placid feet face forward, worshipped and beyond thought, praised by the slender Indra, the Vasus, Rudras, Ādityas, Sādhyas, Aśvins, and the host of the Maruts! O Blessed One, homage to you! Come, come, O Blessed One, endowed with the greatness of the purity and dharma of your own power, valor, splendor, qualities, your own strides, Sāṃkhya, Yoga, and the inner self! Manifest yourself, arise, O Supreme Deity! Shaking all your limbs, wiping away all sins, for the total destruction of those possessed by ruin, O Vidyā of Vidyās, O Supreme Person, O Supreme Auspiciousness, loving to devotees, bestowing fearlessness to grant grace to your devotees! That Brahman, truth, beginningless, unsurpassed, ultimate bliss—let the Blessed One proclaim that; let the Blessed One impart that! Casting away evil, casting away defilement, bring perpetual peace, bring welfare, bring well-being, bring blessing! O Brahman, I surrender to you, O Viṣṇu, O Blessed One, O lotus-eyed one, whose nature consists of the qualities of knowledge, sovereignty, power, strength, and splendor, O Supreme Person, O Supreme Auspiciousness, O Padmanābha, O Hayaśiras, O Primal Boar, O Narasiṃha, O Vāmana, O Trivikrama, O Rāma, O Rāma, O Vāsudeva, O Saṃkarṣaṇa, O Pradyumna, O Aniruddha, O Puruṣa, O Truth, O Scripture, O Vāsudeva, whose deeds are the beginning, middle, and end, whose nature is action, whose self is illusion, who are day and night, ascetic, clad in madder and white garments, Garuḍa, bearing the palm-tree and makara banners, supreme knowledge, having time for your navel! Well-being to us! Well-being to the subjects! / You alone are the mantra, you are protection, you are the unsurpassed remedy. / Deliver me, O Lord of the universe, from threefold suffering as well!

ब्रह्मन्प्रपद्ये त्वां विष्णो शरणागतवत्सल ॥
तदा शुद्धो महामतिर्भवदुःखविनिर्गतः ॥ 2 ॥
इत्युक्तः स च राजेन्द्र ऋषिणा दिव्यचक्षुषा ॥
नमस्कृत्य ऋषेः पादौ सगणः सह राजभिः ॥
प्रदक्षिणमुपाकृत्य प्रविवेश पुरं स्वकम् ॥ 3 ॥
ऋषयस्तेऽप्यनुज्ञाता मार्कण्डेयेन धीमता ॥
नमस्कृत्य हरिं देवं स्वाश्रमं जग्मिरे तदा ॥ 4 ॥
राजापि वज्रो धर्मात्मा मार्कण्डेयेन भाषितम् ॥
पुराणं चिन्तयन्नित्यं नारायणपरायणः ॥
राज्यं च प्राशिषन्नित्यं प्रजा धर्मेण पालयन् ॥ 5 ॥
समाप्तं चेदं विष्णुमहापुराणम ॥
3.71.m:
"O Brahman, I surrender to you, O Viṣṇu, loving to those who seek refuge." / Then, purified and of great wisdom, he became free from the sorrow of worldly existence.
Having been spoken to thus by the sage endowed with divine sight, that best of kings, / having bowed to the feet of the sage together with his retinue and with the kings, / having performed circumambulation, entered his own city.
Those sages as well, having been permitted by the wise Mārkaṇḍeya, / having bowed to the divine Hari, then went to their own hermitage.
And King Vajra, whose nature was righteous, / constantly contemplating the Purāṇa spoken by Mārkaṇḍeya, devoted to Nārāyaṇa, / ruled his kingdom continually, protecting the subjects in accordance with dharma.
And this Viṣṇu Mahāpurāṇa is completed.

3.72.m: Now the Third Book:
1. The presence of the deity through the making and worship of the divine image according to the rules of the Citrasūtra, and from that the fruit of the desired four aims of life.

3.72.s: 2 pratimāsvarūpaniścāyakacitrasūtrasyātodyanṛtyaśāstrajñānāyattatvaṃ tasya ca gītaśāstrādhīnatvaṃ, gītasya tu saṃskṛtaprākṛtāpabhraṣṭādibhedādbāhulyaṃ tatrāpi gadyapadyādibhedapūrvakaṃ śabdaśāstrānusṛtattvam
3.72.d: 2 प्रतिमास्वरूपनिश्चायकचित्रसूत्रस्यातोद्यनृत्यशास्त्रज्ञानायत्तत्वं तस्य च गीतशास्त्राधीनत्वं, गीतस्य तु संस्कृतप्राकृतापभ्रष्टादिभेदाद्बाहुल्यं तत्रापि गद्यपद्यादिभेदपूर्वकं शब्दशास्त्रानुसृतत्त्वम्
3.72.m: 2. The dependence of the Citrasūtra, which determines the nature of an image, upon knowledge of the treatises on instrumental music and dance; and the dependence of that upon the treatise on vocal music; the multiplicity of vocal music through divisions such as Sanskrit, Prakrit, and Apabhraṃśa; and therein, its following of grammar through divisions such as prose and verse.
3. Description of meters beginning with Gāyatrī and Uṣṇih.

4. Description of the ninefold mantras beginning with Ṛg and Yajus, preceded by the speech uttered by oneself, by the sage Ṛcīka, by friend, royal sage, deities, Dānavas, Gandharvas, Rākṣasas, Yakṣas, Kinnaras, and Nāgas.

5. Description of the definition of an aphorism and its fourfold nature, meaning of a sentence, sentence and word and their meaning, the five members, the sixfold commentary on aphorisms, the definition of authoritative persons and the three means of knowledge beginning with perception, the divisions of Nirukta, the Gaṇas, Udgīta, and so forth.
6. Explanation of the methodological devices beginning with subject matter, application, meaning of a category, statement of reason, brief specification, and detailed instruction.
7. The definition of the Prakrit language.
8. The chapter describing synonyms for words beginning with gods...
9. Description of the lexicon.
10. Description of synonyms for human beings and so forth.
11. Indication of feminine words beginning with kīrti in the lexicon.
12. Indication of masculine words beginning with rājan.
13. Statement of neuter words beginning with jala.
14. Statement of figures of speech such as alliteration, chyming, metaphor, and double entendre.
15. Description of the characteristics of Vedic branches, historical accounts, poetry, and epic poetry.
16. Statement of the definition and varieties of riddles.

17. An account of mantras, Brāhmaṇas, Kalpas, and Purāṇas, followed by an account of the characteristics of the twelve types of drama—the nāṭaka, nāṭikā, prakaraṇa, prakaraṇī, samavakāra, īhāmṛga, and the rest—followed by the description of the varieties of heroes and heroines and the aesthetic flavors, beginning with the erotic.

3.72.s: 18 gītasyoraḥkaṇṭhaśiraḥsthānebhyo mandrādisvarotpattiḥ, grāmatrayaṃ, saptasvarāḥ, ekaviṃśatimūrchanāḥ, ekonapañcāśattānāḥ, vṛttitrayam, śrṛṃgārādinavarasānāṃ grāmavibhāgaḥ, daśalakṣaṇā jātayaścatvāro'laṃkārā, aparāntakādigītāni cetigītalakṣaṇavarṇanam
3.72.d: 18 गीतस्योरःकण्ठशिरःस्थानेभ्यो मन्द्रादिस्वरोत्पत्तिः, ग्रामत्रयं, सप्तस्वराः, एकविंशतिमूर्छनाः, एकोनपञ्चाशत्तानाः, वृत्तित्रयम्, श्रृंगारादिनवरसानां ग्रामविभागः, दशलक्षणा जातयश्चत्वारोऽलंकारा, अपरान्तकादिगीतानि चेतिगीतलक्षणवर्णनम्
3.72.m: 18. The arising of the musical notes, beginning with the chest register, from the chest, throat, and head regions; the three basic scales; the seven notes; the twenty-one microtonal scales; the forty-nine melodic sequences; the three styles; the distribution of the scales among the nine aesthetic flavors, beginning with the erotic; the ten characteristics of musical modes; the four ornaments; and songs such as the aparāntaka: this is the description of the characteristics of song.

19. Then, an exposition of the fourfold musical instruments distinguished into wind instruments and the rest, along with an account of the notes, rhythm, varied styles, and percussion instruments, followed by the demonstration of the placement of singers, instrumentalists, and others.

20. Preceded by an exposition of dramatic performance, pure dance, representational dance, the graceful dance, the playhouse, and so forth: a description of the characteristics of gods, demons, kings, their attendants, sages, brahmins, merchants, and others, with suitable costumes, expressive acting, emptyings based on the waist, feet, and so forth, standard gaits, extended gaits, their movement patterns, dance sequences, their dance postures, dramatic styles, and the like.
21. A description of positions for lying down and sitting.
22. A description of the sitting postures and positions such as the relaxed, the slow, the lazy, the stepped, the resting, and the languid.
23. A description of the standing postures for men, distinguished into the Vaiṣṇava, the even-footed, and others.
24. A description of the major limbs.

25. A description of movements of the minor limbs, such as the glances reflecting aesthetic flavors, their application, movements of the eyelids, movements of the pupils, the glance movements distinguished into straight, sidelong, and others, the eyebrow movements following them, nose movements, tongue movements, movements of the lower and upper lips, cheek movements, and tooth movements.
26. Beginning with the distinction between uncombined and combined, the placement of the hands in dance, and the characteristics of hand gestures and their functions.

27. A description of dramatic accessories such as stage properties, bodily decoration, living stage elements, and so forth, according to the fourfold division of acting into verbal, costumed, physical, and temperament-based.

28. The manner of expressing objects of the senses; the representation of bodily gestures through thrills of the limbs and the like, distinguished into agreeable, disagreeable, and neutral; and the representation of dawn, the sky, night, twilight, day, the seasons, clouds, the earth, bodies of water, the cardinal directions, the lunar mansions, and so forth.

29. A description of various movement gaits, such as level with the knees and waist, in circumstances of level knees and waist, natural gait, high-stepping, pride, movement in battle, asceticism, illness, longing, and so on.

3.72.s: 30 śrṛṅgārādinavarasaprakathanaprasaṅgena śrṛṅgārāddhāsyasya raudrātkaruṇasya . vīrādadbhutasya bībhatsādbhayānakasyotpattimabhidhāya tattaddevatāvarṇabhedavyañjanādinirūpaṇam
3.72.d: 30 श्रृङ्गारादिनवरसप्रकथनप्रसङ्गेन श्रृङ्गाराद्धास्यस्य रौद्रात्करुणस्य । वीरादद्भुतस्य बीभत्साद्भयानकस्योत्पत्तिमभिधाय तत्तद्देवतावर्णभेदव्यञ्जनादिनिरूपणम्
3.72.m: 30. In the context of explaining the nine aesthetic flavors beginning with the erotic: stating the emergence of the comic from the erotic, the pathetic from the furious, the wondrous from the heroic, and the terrifying from the loathsome; and the determination of their respective presiding deities, colors, and suggestiveness.
31. An exposition of the forty-nine emotional states, beginning with laughter, love, and grief.
32. A description of the esoteric hand gestures, such as those of the Om̐kāra, water, Vāsudeva, Saṃkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna, and Aniruddha, by means of various arrangements of the fingers.
33. A description of the hand gestures from the dance treatise representing sacred ash, matted hair, Ananta, dharma, knowledge, dispassion, sovereignty, the Goddess, Skanda, and others.
34. A description of the origin of dance and its results, such as enjoyment and liberation.

3.72.s: 35 tapasyatā nārāyaṇenāpsarodarpabhaṃgāya citrakarmaṇorvaśīṃ nirmāya viśvakarmaṇe tatkarmaśikṣaṇaṃ, nṛttānusāraṃ citrepi trailokyānukaraṇaṃ-dṛṣṭibhā vāṃgopāṃgakaravinyāsādikaraṇam, haṃsādipañcapuruṣalakṣaṇāni ca
3.72.d: 35 तपस्यता नारायणेनाप्सरोदर्पभंगाय चित्रकर्मणोर्वशीं निर्माय विश्वकर्मणे तत्कर्मशिक्षणं, नृत्तानुसारं चित्रेपि त्रैलोक्यानुकरणं-दृष्टिभा वांगोपांगकरविन्यासादिकरणम्, हंसादिपञ्चपुरुषलक्षणानि च
3.72.m: 35. Nārāyaṇa, while performing austerities, creating Urvaśī by the art of painting in order to curb the pride of the apsarases, and teaching that craft to Viśvakarman; the imitation of the three worlds even in painting in accordance with dance; the execution of glances, emotional states, major and minor limbs, and hand placements; and the characteristics of the five types of men, beginning with the Haṃsa.
36. In the exposition of the Citrasūtra, the proportions of the limbs of figures, and in accordance with them, the descriptions of the types such as Madhakṣa, Haṃsa, and Mālāvya.
37. The fashioning of women in the art of painting according to the measurements of major and minor limbs.
38. The description of limbs such as the eyes of deities in the art of painting.

39. The nine varieties of the art of painting, accompanied by numerous sub-varieties such as straight, turned sideways, and others, possessing auspicious forms and stances, and conforming to various colors.

40. Preceded by an account of the preparation of the ground suitable for the art of painting, the preparation of colors that last for a long time, and an account of coloring materials such as gold and silver.

41. The fourfold division of painting along with their characteristics, distinguished into the realistic, the lyrical, and others; pictorial defects such as cross-hatching, linear shading, and stippling; pictorial merits such as correct posture and proportion; and the description of the ground and other causes that bring about the destruction of paintings, such as bad seats and ornaments.

42. The execution in painting of gods, kings, sages, gandharvas, daityas, dānavas, and others, armed with weapons and attended by retinue; the fashioning of seats, beds, vehicles, costumes, rivers, oceans, mounts, mountain peaks, the earth with its continents, treasures such as the conch and lotus, and night and twilight accompanied by the moon and lunar mansions, according to specific regions.

3.72.s: 43 citre śrṛṃgārādinavarasapradarśanaṃ, devālayanṛpasabhayostadvimarśaḥ, nidhividyādharahanūmadādimaṃgalyacitrāṇāṃ gṛheṣu yatnāllekhanaṃ svahastenātmagṛhe citralekhananiṣedhacitradoṣaguṇavarṇanam, citrasūtrasamāptiḥ
3.72.d: 43 चित्रे श्रृंगारादिनवरसप्रदर्शनं, देवालयनृपसभयोस्तद्विमर्शः, निधिविद्याधरहनूमदादिमंगल्यचित्राणां गृहेषु यत्नाल्लेखनं स्वहस्तेनात्मगृहे चित्रलेखननिषेधचित्रदोषगुणवर्णनम्, चित्रसूत्रसमाप्तिः
3.72.m: 43. The demonstration of the nine aesthetic flavors beginning with the erotic in painting; their evaluation in temples and royal courts; the careful depiction in houses of auspicious paintings such as treasures, vidyādharas, and Hanumat; the prohibition against painting with one's own hand in one's own house; the description of the defects and merits of painting; and the conclusion of the Citrasūtra.
44. A description of the rules for creating images of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śaṅkara.
45. A description of the fashioning of the lotus suitable for the worship of Viṣṇu.

3.72.s: 46 arūpasyāpi devasya vikṛtivaśātsākāratā, tatra ca brahmaṇaḥ sahetukaṃ caturvaktratādinirūpaṇam
3.72.d: 46 अरूपस्यापि देवस्य विकृतिवशात्साकारता, तत्र च ब्रह्मणः सहेतुकं चतुर्वक्त्रतादिनिरूपणम्
3.72.m: 46. The embodied nature of God, though formless, through the power of transformation; and therein, the reasoned exposition of Brahmā's four-faced nature and the like.

3.72.s: 47 viṣṇurūpanirmāṇe caturbāhūnāñcaturdiktvaṃ, caturvaktrāṇāñca balajñānaiśvaryaśaktirūpatā, balasyāpi vāsudevasaṅkarṣaṇapradyumnāniruddhatā, vāsudevasya prativaktraṃ sūryacandrarūpaṃ karadvayam, saṃkarṣaṇādirūpāṇāmapi musalalāṅgalādyāyudhatādivarṇanam
3.72.d: 47 विष्णुरूपनिर्माणे चतुर्बाहूनाञ्चतुर्दिक्त्वं, चतुर्वक्त्राणाञ्च बलज्ञानैश्वर्यशक्तिरूपता, बलस्यापि वासुदेवसङ्कर्षणप्रद्युम्नानिरुद्धता, वासुदेवस्य प्रतिवक्त्रं सूर्यचन्द्ररूपं करद्वयम्, संकर्षणादिरूपाणामपि मुसललाङ्गलाद्यायुधतादिवर्णनम्
3.72.m: 47. In the fashioning of the form of Viṣṇu, the four arms representing the four cardinal directions; the four faces being the forms of strength, knowledge, sovereignty, and energy; the identification of strength with Vāsudeva, Saṃkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna, and Aniruddha; for each face of Vāsudeva, two hands in the form of the sun and the moon; and the description of the forms of Saṃkarṣaṇa and the others possessing weapons such as the pestle and the plough.

3.72.s: 48 mahādevasya sadyojāta vāmadevādibhedena pañcavaktrāṇi prativaktraṃ somasūryāgninetratrayatvam, bhūmyāditatvāni, viśuddhajñānavairāgyādīnāmādarśādirūpatā
3.72.d: 48 महादेवस्य सद्योजात वामदेवादिभेदेन पञ्चवक्त्राणि प्रतिवक्त्रं सोमसूर्याग्निनेत्रत्रयत्वम्, भूम्यादितत्वानि, विशुद्धज्ञानवैराग्यादीनामादर्शादिरूपता
3.72.m: 48. The five faces of Mahādeva, distinguished into Sadyojāta, Vāmadeva, and the rest; each face possessing the three eyes of the moon, sun, and fire; the cosmic elements beginning with earth; and pure knowledge, dispassion, and the rest taking forms such as the mirror.
49. The fashioning of the forms of the Nāsatyas.
50. The fashioning of the forms of Śakra and Śacī, along with its symbolic reasons.

3.72.s: 51 sahetukaṃ yamarūpanirūpaṇaṃ tasya saṃkarṣaṇarūpatā, tadvāhanamahiṣasya moharūpatvaṃ dhūmorṇāsvarūpaṃ citraguptasvarūpakathanādi ca
3.72.d: 51 सहेतुकं यमरूपनिरूपणं तस्य संकर्षणरूपता, तद्वाहनमहिषस्य मोहरूपत्वं धूमोर्णास्वरूपं चित्रगुप्तस्वरूपकथनादि च
3.72.m: 51. The reasoned determination of the form of Yama, his identity with Saṃkarṣaṇa, his buffalo mount having the nature of delusion, the nature of Dhūmorṇā, the account of the nature of Citragupta, and so forth.

3.72.s: 52 saśaktikasāyudhasavāhanavaruṇasvarūpaṃ, taddakṣiṇabhāge makaravāhanagaṅgāsvarūpam, vāmabhāge sacāmarakūrmasthayamunāsvarūpam, varuṇasya pradyumnatā tadbhāryāyā ratirūpatādikathanañca
3.72.d: 52 सशक्तिकसायुधसवाहनवरुणस्वरूपं, तद्दक्षिणभागे मकरवाहनगङ्गास्वरूपम्, वामभागे सचामरकूर्मस्थयमुनास्वरूपम्, वरुणस्य प्रद्युम्नता तद्भार्याया रतिरूपतादिकथनञ्च
3.72.m: 52. The form of Varuṇa accompanied by his consort, weapons, and mount; on his right side, the form of Gaṅgā riding a makara; on his left side, the form of Yamunā standing on a tortoise, bearing a fly-whisk; and the account of Varuṇa being Pradyumna and his wife being Rati.

3.72.s: 53 dhanadasvarūpanirmāṇam, tasya vāmāṃge ṛddhiḥ, śaṃkhapadmanidhyādi tatpārśve,
3.72.d: 53 धनदस्वरूपनिर्माणम्, तस्य वामांगे ऋद्धिः, शंखपद्मनिध्यादि तत्पार्श्वे,
3.72.m: 53. The fashioning of the form of Dhanada, with Ṛddhi on his left side, and treasures such as the conch and lotus at his side.
54. The fashioning of the form of Garuḍa.
55. The fashioning of the image of Gaurīśa.
56. The fashioning of the form of Agni accompanied by Svāhā, together with representations such as parrots having the form of the four Vedas.
57. The fashioning of the form of Virūpākṣa, along with dance and the like.
58. The fashioning of Vāyu, sky-colored, accompanied by his consort.
59. The manner of fashioning the forms of Bhairava and Mahākāla.
60. Another form of Viṣṇu, who possesses a single wheel, has two arms, and holds a mace and a discus.
61. The creation of the form of Bhūdevī, of white complexion, four-armed, holding in her hands jewels, crops, herbs, a lotus, and other [attributes].
62. The form of space (Ākāśa), possessing garments resembling a blue lotus.
63. The distinguishing characteristics of the forms of Brahmā and Sāvitrī.
64. The creation of the form of Sarasvatī, which accomplishes all aims for the meditator.
65. The description of the form of Ananta (Śeṣa).
66. The creation of Tumburu, like Mahādeva, accompanied by the goddesses Jayā, Vijayā, Jayantī, and Aparājitā.

3.72.s: 67 prakāradvayena piṃgalātipiṃgalagaṇayuktasya revantādicatuṣputraiścatasṛbhiḥ patnībhiśca sahitasya rave rūpanirmāṇam
3.72.d: 67 प्रकारद्वयेन पिंगलातिपिंगलगणयुक्तस्य रेवन्तादिचतुष्पुत्रैश्चतसृभिः पत्नीभिश्च सहितस्य रवे रूपनिर्माणम्
3.72.m: 67. The creation of the form of the Sun in two ways: endowed with the attendants Piṅgala and Atipiṅgala, and accompanied by his four sons, Revanta and the others, and by his four wives.

3.72.s: 68 sitakumudahastasya kāntiśobhābhyāṃ bhāryābhyāṃ sahitasyāśvinyādyaṣṭāviṃśatibhāryābhirvā sahitasya candramaso nirmāṇam
3.72.d: 68 सितकुमुदहस्तस्य कान्तिशोभाभ्यां भार्याभ्यां सहितस्याश्विन्याद्यष्टाविंशतिभार्याभिर्वा सहितस्य चन्द्रमसो निर्माणम्
3.72.m: 68. The creation of the Moon, who holds a white water-lily in his hand, accompanied by his two wives Kānti and Śobhā, or accompanied by his twenty-eight wives beginning with Aśvinī.
69. The creation of the planets, beginning with Mars, along with their weapons and mounts.
70. The creation of the forms of the present and future Manus.
71. The creation of the forms of Skanda, Viśākha, Guha, Bhadrakālī, Brahmā, Gaṇeśa, and Viśvakarman.
72. The description of the forms of the Vasus beginning with Dharā, and of Viṣṇu, Indra, Varuṇa, and the others.
73. The creation of Kaśyapa and others, followed by Kāṣṭhā and others, and of numerous deities such as Dhruva, Agastya, Bhṛgu, and Kubera.
74. The creation of the form of the liṅga.
75. The creation of the form of the firmament.
76. The creation of the forms of Nara and Nārāyaṇa beside the jujube tree.
77. The creation of the form of Dharma, accompanied by his fourteen wives beginning with Kīrti.
78. The creation of the image of Nṛsiṃha in three ways.

79. The creation of the man-boar (Nṛvarāha), who represents sovereignty, who is ready to sever the head of Hiraṇyākṣa representing absence of sovereignty, and who is accompanied by the goddess Earth (Dharaṇī).
80. The creation of the form of Hayagrīva […].
81. The creation of the form of [Viṣṇu] reclining upon Śeṣa.
82. The manner of creating the painted form of Lakṣmī, both at the side of Viṣṇu and separately […].
83. The description of the universal form of Hari.
84. The creation of the form of an aiḍūka.

3.72.s: 85 vāsudevarūpanirmāṇe sāyudhasapārṣadasaśaktikasya viṣṇoścaturmukhādibhedena rūpanirmāṇaṃ tathā bhārgavarāmadāśarathirāmādi (devodyāna ) mūrtinirmāṇam
3.72.d: 85 वासुदेवरूपनिर्माणे सायुधसपार्षदसशक्तिकस्य विष्णोश्चतुर्मुखादिभेदेन रूपनिर्माणं तथा भार्गवरामदाशरथिरामादि (देवोद्यान ) मूर्तिनिर्माणम्
3.72.m: 85. In the creation of the form of Vāsudeva, the creation of the form of Viṣṇu accompanied by weapons, attendants, and Śaktis according to the divisions of four faces and so forth; likewise, the creation of the images of Bhārgava Rāma, Dāśarathi Rāma, and others (in divine groves).
86. The description of temples named Himavat and so forth, and the installation therein of images of Sarvatobhadra, Keśava, and others.
87. The installation of images of Vāsudeva, Saṃkarṣaṇa, and others in order beginning from the east, in a temple equipped with a pavilion, doorway, spire, and other features.

88. In a temple (standard temple) of sixty-four squares, the description of the measurements of the doorway, image, pedestal, waist, floor, spire, inner chamber, door, wall, floor, walkways, steps, and other parts.
89. The examination of timber for a temple.

3.72.s: 90 dāruparīkṣoktavidhivacchaile daivajña purohitābhyāṃ devārcārhaśilāparīkṣaṇaṃ, śilānāmuttamamadhyamanikṛṣṭatādibhedena tāsāṃ phalāni pākena tāsāṃ dārḍhyakaraṇañca
3.72.d: 90 दारुपरीक्षोक्तविधिवच्छैले दैवज्ञ पुरोहिताभ्यां देवार्चार्हशिलापरीक्षणं, शिलानामुत्तममध्यमनिकृष्टतादिभेदेन तासां फलानि पाकेन तासां दार्ढ्यकरणञ्च
3.72.m: 90. Just as in the rule stated for the examination of timber, the examination of stone fit for worship of the deity in the mountain by the astrologer and the royal priest; the results of the stones according to their classification as superior, middling, and inferior; and making them firm through firing.
91. Bringing clay according to the distinction of the classes beginning with the brahmins, and the making of bricks for the temple of a deity by brahmins and the others.
92. The methods of making adamant mortar (vajralepa) using substances such as binduka, wood-apple, mango, flowers of the silk-cotton tree, and others.

3.72.s: 93 satyayuge devānāṃ pratyakṣapūjanaṃ tretādvāparayoḥ pratyakṣapūjā pratimāsu ca, tatrāpi tretāyuge gṛhe dvāpara cāraṇye kalau ca devāyatananirmitirnagareṣu samārabdhā, bhūmidānaṃ vidhāyeva devāyatanapratiṣṭhā kāryā, devālayayogyabhūmiḥ
3.72.d: 93 सत्ययुगे देवानां प्रत्यक्षपूजनं त्रेताद्वापरयोः प्रत्यक्षपूजा प्रतिमासु च, तत्रापि त्रेतायुगे गृहे द्वापर चारण्ये कलौ च देवायतननिर्मितिर्नगरेषु समारब्धा, भूमिदानं विधायेव देवायतनप्रतिष्ठा कार्या, देवालययोग्यभूमिः
3.72.m: 93. The direct worship of the gods in the Kṛta age; direct worship and [worship] in images in the Tretā and Dvāpara ages; even then, [worship] in the home in the Tretā age, in the forest in the Dvāpara, and in the Kali age the building of temples was commenced in cities; the installation of a temple should only be performed after making a gift of land; land suitable for a temple.

3.72.s: 94 brāhmaṇādivarṇoktamṛdi bhūśodhanapurassaraṃ śalyoddhārādi vidhāya śrī-viṣṇuvāstudevādipūjanaṃ kāryam, aiśānyāṃ śilāṃ vinyasya prādakṣiṇyena punastannyāsaṃ samācaret. tadahareva sūtranyāsanandādiśilārcanaṃ vidhāya citrakarma vidheyaṃ viṣṇavādiprāsāde garuḍādeṣuściddhānyapi kartavyāni.
3.72.d: 94 ब्राह्मणादिवर्णोक्तमृदि भूशोधनपुरस्सरं शल्योद्धारादि विधाय श्री-विष्णुवास्तुदेवादिपूजनं कार्यम्, ऐशान्यां शिलां विन्यस्य प्रादक्षिण्येन पुनस्तन्न्यासं समाचरेत्। तदहरेव सूत्रन्यासनन्दादिशिलार्चनं विधाय चित्रकर्म विधेयं विष्णवादिप्रासादे गरुडादेषुश्चिद्धान्यपि कर्तव्यानि।
3.72.m: 94. Having purified the ground in clay prescribed for the classes beginning with the brahmins and having performed the extraction of subterranean faults and other rites, the worship of Śrī, Viṣṇu, Vāstudeva, and other deities is to be performed; having laid a stone in the northeast, one should then perform its placement in clockwise succession. On that very day, having performed the placement of the cord and the worship of the stone Nandā and others, painting should be undertaken; on a temple of Viṣṇu and others, marks of Garuḍa and the like must also be made.

3.72.s: 95 vāstupuruṣe śalyajñānaṃ, śalyaṃ vihāya vāstudevāyatanaṃ kartavyam, devāyatanadīkṣaṇādibhāgeṣu devatākośabhavanādi, dhanaśalye labdhe vṛddhiḥ .
3.72.d: 95 वास्तुपुरुषे शल्यज्ञानं, शल्यं विहाय वास्तुदेवायतनं कर्तव्यम्, देवायतनदीक्षणादिभागेषु देवताकोशभवनादि, धनशल्ये लब्धे वृद्धिः ।
3.72.m: 95. Knowledge of subterranean faults in the site-person (vāstupuruṣa); avoiding subterranean faults, a temple for the site-deity is to be constructed; in the sections such as the viewing of the temple, the treasury-chamber of the deity and so forth; when a subterranean fault of wealth is obtained, there is increase.

3.72.s: 96 vaiṣṇavādiyugeṣvāśvinyādinakṣatreṣu saṃvatsarādiṣu varṣeṣu vasantādyṛtuṣu māghādimāseṣu sūryādivāreṣu pratipadāditithiṣu śakunādikaraṇeṣu meṣādilagneṣu sūryādihorāsu pratiṣṭhāphalāni
3.72.d: 96 वैष्णवादियुगेष्वाश्विन्यादिनक्षत्रेषु संवत्सरादिषु वर्षेषु वसन्ताद्यृतुषु माघादिमासेषु सूर्यादिवारेषु प्रतिपदादितिथिषु शकुनादिकरणेषु मेषादिलग्नेषु सूर्यादिहोरासु प्रतिष्ठाफलानि
3.72.m: 96. The fruits of installation in the ages beginning with the Vaiṣṇava, under the lunar asterisms beginning with Aśvinī, in years beginning with the saṃvatsara, in seasons beginning with spring, in months beginning with Māgha, on days of the week beginning with Sunday, on lunar days beginning with the first, in astrological divisions beginning with śakuni, in ascendants beginning with Aries, and in planetary hours beginning with that of the Sun.

97. In the explanation of the rule of installation, the patron's taking of initiation together with the priests, preceded by the recitation of auspicious verses, the tying of the protective thread and bracelet, and the description of the vows such as giving up meat and liquor, and eating sacrificial food.

98. In a temple constructed according to rule, in the western and other sections of the preliminary-dwelling mound, preceded by the entry of the Kalpaka and other [priests], the installation of water-pots, setting up of archways, banners, canopies, water-clocks, and door-guardians, proper adornment with bells, mirrors, and so on, and the protection of the sacrifice with demon-slaying mantras.
99. The consecration with the five bovine products.
100. The description of the rule of purification of the image.
101. The description of preliminary dwelling (adhivāsana).
102. The description of the rule of preliminary dwelling of life and so forth, along with mantras and their initial words.
103. The invocations of the gods beginning with the Nāsatyas.
104. The proclamation of the mantras for invocation, guest-water, foot-water, incense, and other [offerings] for the gods beginning with Brahmā.
105. The invocation of the Bull of the Worlds, the Trident, Nandīśvara, and others.

106. The description of the invocation and worship of Śrī, Viṣṇu, his various incarnations, and other deities, of the Pāṇḍavas beginning with Yudhiṣṭhira, and of Draupadī, Sītā, Devakī, Yaśodā, Rukmiṇī, and others.
107. The awakening mantras of Śrī Vāsudeva.
108. The fashioning of the image and the invocation of Viṣṇu, whose form is manifest and unmanifest, for ease of meditation and for the sake of enjoyment and liberation.
109. The description of the rule of fire offerings.
110. The description of the awakening mantras of the Blessed Lord.
111. The description of the materials, mantras, and greatness of the great bath.
112. The description of the offering of enjoyment, such as the anointing with perfumes and the presenting of a palm-leaf fan.
113. The offering of the honey-mixture.
114. The offering of sacrificial food, such as edible and chewable things, preceded by the offering of hospitality to Śrī Viṣṇu.
115. The description of the worship according to the Sātvata [tradition] by the rule proclaimed in the song of Śaṅkara.
116. The description of the rule for the removal of the archways […].

3.72.s: 117 tattaddevatātithiṣu prathamādipañcamadivasaparyantaṃ vināyakagraharkṣanāgapramatha brāhmaṇapūjanāni ṣaṣṭhe'hni ca bṛhatsnapanaṃ kartavyam . tatra sarveṣāṃ nāgarikāṇāṃ rājñā saha mahanā vādyaghoṣeṇa nṛtyagītādimaṃgalaistutibhiścānugamanaṃ nimittadarśanañca
3.72.d: 117 तत्तद्देवतातिथिषु प्रथमादिपञ्चमदिवसपर्यन्तं विनायकग्रहर्क्षनागप्रमथ ब्राह्मणपूजनानि षष्ठेऽह्नि च बृहत्स्नपनं कर्तव्यम् । तत्र सर्वेषां नागरिकाणां राज्ञा सह महना वाद्यघोषेण नृत्यगीतादिमंगलैस्तुतिभिश्चानुगमनं निमित्तदर्शनञ्च
3.72.m: 117. On the lunar days of the respective deities, up to the fifth day from the first, the worship of Vināyaka, the planets, the lunar asterisms, the serpent-deities, the Pramathas, and the brahmins [is to be performed], and on the sixth day the great bath is to be carried out; there, the following along of all the citizens together with the king with the loud sound of musical instruments, with auspicious songs, dances, and praises, and the observation of omens.
118. The worship of Aniruddha, Saṃkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna, Vāsudeva, and others according to desires such as dharma, wealth, pleasure, and liberation.
119 Worship of Matsya, Varāha, Hayagrīva, and others according to desires such as voyages by sea vessels, crossing rivers, and beginning study.
120 Determination of the time of worship for Hayagrīva and other deities.

3.72.s: 216 phālgunapūrṇamāyāṃ lakṣmīnārāyaṇāvindurātrirūpiṇāvabhyarcya caitravaiśākhajyeṣṭhamāseṣu ca tathaivābhyarcyaikaṃ pāraṇam. āṣāḍhaśrāvaṇabhādrapadāśvinamāseṣu śriyā saha śrīdharaṃ sampūjya candramasaḥ pūjanena dvitīyaṃ pāraṇam .. kārttikādimāseṣu keśavamarcayitvā bhūmicandramasoḥ pūjanena tṛtīyaṃ pāraṇam . etatpāraṇatraye prathamapāraṇe pañcagavyaprāśanaṃ, dvitīye kuśodakaṃ, tṛtīye sūryāṃśutaptañjalamiti niyamena lakṣmīnārāyaṇau sampūjya naro naiṣṭairviyujyate'ntakāle labhate ca devasmṛtiṃ muktiñca tata iti
3.72.d: 216 फाल्गुनपूर्णमायां लक्ष्मीनारायणाविन्दुरात्रिरूपिणावभ्यर्च्य चैत्रवैशाखज्येष्ठमासेषु च तथैवाभ्यर्च्यैकं पारणम्। आषाढश्रावणभाद्रपदाश्विनमासेषु श्रिया सह श्रीधरं सम्पूज्य चन्द्रमसः पूजनेन द्वितीयं पारणम् ॥ कार्त्तिकादिमासेषु केशवमर्चयित्वा भूमिचन्द्रमसोः पूजनेन तृतीयं पारणम् । एतत्पारणत्रये प्रथमपारणे पञ्चगव्यप्राशनं, द्वितीये कुशोदकं, तृतीये सूर्यांशुतप्तञ्जलमिति नियमेन लक्ष्मीनारायणौ सम्पूज्य नरो नैष्टैर्वियुज्यतेऽन्तकाले लभते च देवस्मृतिं मुक्तिञ्च तत इति
3.72.m: 216. Having worshipped Lakṣmī and Nārāyaṇa in the forms of the moon and night on the full moon day of Phālguna, and having worshipped likewise in the months of Caitra, Vaiśākha, and Jyeṣṭha, there is one breaking of the fast; having worshipped Śrīdhara together with Śrī in the months of Āṣāḍha, Śrāvaṇa, Bhādrapada, and Āśvina, the second breaking of the fast is with the worship of the moon; having worshipped Keśava in the months beginning with Kārttika, the third breaking of the fast is with the worship of the earth and the moon. In these three breakings of the fast, by consuming the five products of the cow at the first, kuśa-water at the second, and water heated by the sun's rays at the third according to rule, having worshipped Lakṣmī and Nārāyaṇa, a person is not separated from loved ones, and at the end of life attains remembrance of the deity and thereby liberation.
